blocks.text: Build Websites Without Writing Code

Ever thought about building your own website — for a portfolio, a side project, or just for fun? The problem is, it usually takes developers and days of work. This's where Lovable changes everything by building websites using AI — quickly and easily! So, in this guide, you'll learn what Lovable is, who it's for, and how to use it. Let's start!
What is Lovable?
Before diving into the topic, let's start with a quick quiz.

blocks.text: So, Lovable is an AI-powered platform that converts your ideas into functional websites. Here's how it works:

• You describe what you need in plain language
  • Lovable generates the structure, layout, and basic functionality
And the coolest part: Lovable does it all automatically.
How Lovable Works?

Every project starts with writing your first prompt on Lovable's home page, and then it will give you the first version of the website that you asked for. This makes the process from idea to prototype fast and efficient.
As a result, you can focus on your vision and skip a myriad of complex technical steps that are required by traditional development!

For example, you could ask for a simple portfolio site with an "About" section and a "Project Gallery".

Then, Lovable will generate the structure, add placeholders, and show a working preview you can refine.
Thus, Lovable empowers anyone with ideas but no coding skills — from entrepreneurs to creators — to quickly bring their visions to life.
When to Use Lovable
Lovable is perfect for fast and functional builds. Let's take a look at some examples.
Business Websites

For example, if you have a small cafe, you might want a website showing your menu, location, and opening hours.

Lovable can build that for you — just describe what you need, and get a clean, functional site without hiring a developer!
Landing Pages

Another example: You're planning to build and sell an online course about your profession and need a page to collect email signups before the launch date.

With Lovable, describe what you need — a home page with course benefits, email capture form, and testimonials — and get a working page in minutes!
Portfolio Sites

Imagine you need a website that will showcase your work professionally to potential clients, as a freelance photographer. Lovable can help you with it too!

It build a portfolio with project galleries, an "About" section, and a contact form — so you can focus on your photography, not learning web development!
Hence, whether you're launching services or creating a website for your business, Lovable will help you to do it fast before committing significant resources!
When Lovable Isn't the Best Choice

Last but not least, it is also important to know Lovable's limits — it will help you understand if it's the right tool for you.

So, remember that while Lovable is great for straightforward projects, some ideas need traditional development.
For example, building something like an online store where customers create accounts, make payments, and track orders — that level of complexity goes beyond what Lovable is designed for.

In this lesson, you'll learn how to turn a simple idea into a live site by describing what you want in simple language.

Along the way, you'll explore how to write clear prompts, preview results instantly, and tweak them in real time. So, let's bring concepts to life!
Starting Simple

As it was mentioned in the first lesson, every website begins with one prompt. In these terms, it is similar to describing an idea to a friend. No technical terms or perfect wording — just type what you want into the text field on Lovable's home page.
When writing a prompt, start with what you're building and who it's for. Don't overthink it — just communicate the core idea. You can always refine the result later.
Here's a couple of examples:

• "Build a personal portfolio site"
  • "Create a landing page for my coffee shop"
The key here is clarity and simplicity.

blocks.text: The Preview Window

As soon as your site is generated, you'll see your website in the preview window.

This is a live, interactive version of your site that will update in real time as you make changes.
Making Your First Edit
Want to adjust something? Just describe the change in the "Chat" section. You can edit sections, colors, pages, or structure — all in plain language.
For example, when you want to change the structure, you can tell Lovable what sections you need and where. For example:

• "Add a contact form"
  • "Create a services page"
  • "Move the portfolio above the about section"
Thus, every update will build on your current version.
Structural and Visual Changes
To edit effectively, you should know the difference between structural changes and visual changes:

• Structural changes affect what's on the page — like adding a new section, removing a page, or reordering content.
  • Visual changes affect how things look — like colors, fonts, spacing, and style.

feedbackCorrect.text: Perfect! Adding or removing sections changes the structure — what exists on the page and how it's organized. Visual changes only affect how existing elements look.

feedbackIncorrect.text: That's actually a visual change. Structural changes involve adding, removing, or reorganizing sections and content areas, while visual changes modify the appearance of existing elements.

options.label: Changing the button color from blue to green
Adding a testimonials section below the about page
Adjusting the spacing between paragraphs
Increasing the font size of headlines

blocks.question: Considering this, which of these is a structural change rather than a visual design change?

blocks.text: Hence, when making visual changes, you need to be specific by mentioning such aspects as:

• Colors
  • Fonts
  • Styles
This way, Lovable will know exactly what you want.
Example prompt might look like this:

• "Make the header background dark blue with white text"
  • "Use a modern, minimal font throughout"

Also, you may make both structural and visual changes together. This is perfectly fine — just be clear about what you're adjusting. For instance: "Add a pricing section with three tiers and use a modern gradient background."

blocks.prompt: Now that you know the difference, complete this prompt to make a structural change to your site.
blocks.template: Add a [type] section with [number] below [position].

blocks.prompt: Next, complete the prompt to change the visual style.
blocks.template: Change [element] to [color] and make [element] [style].

blocks.text: Well Done!
See how this works? You describe what you want changed — whether it's structure, visuals, or both — and Lovable updates your site accordingly.
Overall, the core insight from this lesson is that building websites with Lovable is iterative: you start broad, then refine. Each prompt improves your website until it matches your vision.
A typical workflow looks like this: start with your structure → add or move sections, refine the visuals → adjust the small details. This way, you see progress quickly while staying in control!

Sometimes you already have a design in mind — maybe a designer created mockups for you, or you've seen a website you love and want something similar. Turning those visuals into a real, working website usually means hiring a developer.

With Lovable, you can skip that step by importing your designs directly and watch them become functional websites. Let's see how!
Why Import Designs?

Designers create beautiful, polished visuals. AI builds structure and functionality fast. 

Importing designs into Lovable lets you combine both — keeping the look your designer intended while Lovable handles the technical side

3 Ways to Import
Lovable gives you multiple options for bringing designs to life:

• Screenshots — from any design tool
  • Figma plugin — direct integration via Builder.io
  • Website cloning — capturing and recreating existing sites
Let's explore how each method suits different workflows!
Method 1: Screenshots
The simplest approach: take screenshots of any design and drop them into Lovable. These might be:

• A screenshot from a design tool
  • A saved image from Pinterest
  • Even a photo of a sketch on paper
Lovable will analyze the visual layout and recreate it as a working website

blocks.text: Method 2: Figma Plugin
If your designer works in Figma (or you use it yourself), there's a direct connection through Builder.io that makes importing even smoother.
Here's how it works:

1. Structure your Figma design with Auto Layout and clear layer names (your designer can set this up).
  2. Install the Builder.io plugin in Figma.
  3. Select the frames you want to import.
  4. Click 'Open in Lovable.'
Your design will become a functional app instantly!

blocks.text: Planning with Notion

Once you brainstormed your ideas, start planning your projects in Notion. 

There, you can write down features, describe what your pages should include, or sketch quick outlines.

This clarification step helps you know exactly what to ask Lovable to build.

Then, because Lovable understands plain language, you can practically copy-paste a well-written project description into it as a prompt!
For instance, your workflow might look like this:

1. Outline feature list in Notion.
  2. Clean it up into clear, simple descriptions.
  3. Copy that text as your Lovable prompt.
Hence, your note-taking tool becomes the place you draft what Lovable will build.
Design with Figma
Remember Figma from the previous lesson? Such professional design tools work in tandem with Lovable.

Sketch your website layout in Figma or even on paper. Lovable will import the actual design via Figma integration or interpret a screenshot and turn it into a working website.

This way, your visual design tools ensure aesthetics meet your vision — Lovable handles the coding and assembly.

Lovable generates short placeholder text like generic headings or labels. 

But it doesn't know your brand voice or marketing goals.
For important copy — landing page headlines, "About" page text, product descriptions — craft those carefully in ChatGPT or Jasper.
Example prompt for ChatGPT: "I'm a creative graphic designer. Give me a hero section headline and subheading for a personal portfolio site."
Once you have copy you like, paste it into Lovable. You can either:

• Edit text directly on the page.
  • Or use a prompt like "Change the tagline to Designing a better world, one pixel at a time."

Your hero section makes first impressions. It needs three elements:

• Clear headline — what you do

Writing Effective CTAs
Call-to-action copy should be specific and action-oriented. Tell visitors exactly what happens next and what benefit they get.
Instead of generic "Click Here" or "Submit," use:

• "Get Your Free Quote"
  • "Start Building Today"
  • "Download the Guide"
